newsitem.title: USA: Amgen, Genentech report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Amgen, Genentech report higher earnings.

text.p: Biotechnology giant Amgen Inc. Tuesday reported a healthy rise in second-quarter profits despite a significant slowdown in the rate of growth of one of its two key drugs.

The Thousand Oaks, Calif.-based company said second-quarter net income rose 12 percent to $200.5 million, or 72 cents a share, from $178.7 million, or 64 cents per share, in the year-ago second quarter. Total revenues were up 9 percent to $620.5 million from $571.4 million a year ago.
In another earnings report by a major biotechnology company, Genentech Inc. said second-quarter profits rose 10 percent to $23.8 million, or 19 cents per share, from $21.7 million, or 18 cents.
New Medicare reimbursement policies cut into the sales of Amgen's Epogen drug, which rose 12 percent in the latest quarter, compared with a 19 percent growth rate in the prior quarter.

Under the new Medicare policy, patients will have to meet stricter standards for their insurance plan to cover Epogen, which boosts the red blood cell count and is widely prescribed to people on kidney dialysis.

However, Amgen said it believes it saw the worst impact of these changes in the second quarter, when some doctors responded by immediately taking their patients off the drug. It expects sales growth rates to recover to around 15 percent in the second half of the year, as some of the patients taken off the drug see their red blood cell counts drop to levels that would again qualify them for reimbursement.
In an interview after earnings were reported, Amgen Chairman Gordon Binder said he thinks the new regulations will only affect a small percentage of patients in the future.

The changes in the reimbursement policies have been closely watched by investors who feared the change could significantly cut into sales of Epogen, which now accounts for more than half of Amgen's total sales.

Recent weakness in Amgen's stock price has been widely linked to the Medicare policy changes, as well as to studies questioning the benefits of its other drug, Neupogen, a white blood cell agent given to cancer chemotherapy patients.
Amgen stock rose $1.875 to $57.25 Tuesday before earnings were reported, but remains well off the high for the year of about $69 per share.

Investors have also expressed concern over the new leptin drug Amgen is developing for obesity. The project has been the subject of considerable hype, but trial data released in June suggested it may not be the wonder drug overweight people had been hoping for. The trial showed leptin produced some weight loss but not as much as some competing diet drugs already on the market.

In its earnings report, Genentech said its higher earnings mainly reflected a change in its tax rate, and that its sales fell slightly to $233.5 million from $243.8 million in last year's second quarter.

Contributing to the decline in sales was the company's heart attack and stroke drug, Activase, whose revenues were hurt by new competitive drugs on the market, and a shift by some patients away from drugs in favor of medical devices to correct blockages.
